lead.headline: Leave room for the evening
lead.body: Start with a short Mornington foreshore out-and-back, then keep dinner in town. Set your turn-back time before leaving and check the forecast and access. If the wind or rain wins, make it a table-led evening instead.

picks.headline: Read the other coast
picks.body: Western Port Writes runs at Coolart on 10 and 11 October, with a Somers opening on Friday. Choose one session and plan your picnic before you leave.
picks.label: Choose a festival session

picks.headline: A fresh pour for October
picks.body: Jetty Road’s Oktoberfest runs from 9 to 11 October, with German-inspired brews and a special Hoppy German release. Keep the brewery as your one stop for the afternoon.
picks.label: See the brewery programme

editorial.headline: The case for a spring weekend
editorial.body: Spring changes the shape of a Peninsula weekend. Our seasonal story makes the case for doing less, choosing a base and leaving room for the coast.
editorial.label: Explore the spring story

standfirst: October brought a reason to walk together. This weekend’s shape is simple: one good commitment, then time left over.

lead.headline: Walk for something close to home
lead.body: Choose the 5km or 10km community walk, finishing at Rosebud Village Green. The organiser says profit after event costs supports locals undergoing breast cancer treatment. Register first, then leave the afternoon open rather than adding another cross-Peninsula drive.

picks.headline: Fold something worth keeping
picks.body: Artist Jacky Cheng leads a tessellation-folding workshop at MPRG, 9:30am to 12:30pm. Check places before making this your morning, then leave time for the exhibition.

picks.headline: Let Sunday stay in the garden
picks.body: The rose gardens list high tea for Sunday 18 October. Check booking availability first and give the afternoon one destination rather than a list of stops.
picks.label: Check high tea bookings

editorial.headline: A gallery afternoon, properly planned
editorial.body: National Works on Paper runs until 22 November. Our practical spring guide helps you shape a visit to MPRG, with time to look rather than rushing through on the way somewhere else.

lead.place: Point Nepean to Martha Cove · EXPLORE
lead.headline: Give the coast a whole day
lead.body: Sunday’s supported 35km route starts at Quarantine Station and finishes at Martha Cove Marina. If you’ve trained for it, check registration and shuttle details before committing; supporters should follow the organiser’s route guidance. Prefer a shorter day? The walking story below is the useful alternative.

picks.headline: Bring the sea into the kitchen
picks.body: The destination calendar lists a Sensational Seafood workshop at Peninsula Gourmet Cooking School on 25 October, 11am to 3pm. Check operator availability before building your Sunday around it.
picks.label: Check the cooking programme

picks.headline: Save the coast for tomorrow
picks.body: Keep Saturday indoors at National Works on Paper, then have lunch in Mornington. The exhibition continues through 22 November, so you can give it time without racing another deadline.
picks.label: Plan the gallery visit

editorial.headline: A shorter walk, with a better finish
editorial.body: Not every coastal day needs 35 kilometres. Our late-afternoon walking story helps you choose a smaller outing, then leave enough light for the return and dinner nearby. Check current access and conditions before setting off.
editorial.label: Choose the shorter walk

standfirst: October left a longer weekend within reach. The useful decision came first: choose the base, then choose how much to do.

lead.place: Red Hill to the coast · STAY
lead.headline: Let the weekend widen
lead.body: Start on the ridge with Montalto, then let the coast shape the next day. The two-night plan puts accommodation and dining decisions first, with park access and weather checked before each walk. Cup Day is Tuesday 3 November; Monday still needs its own leave decision.

picks.headline: See where the work begins
picks.body: MPRG’s Local artists at work studio tour is listed for Friday 30 October, 9:30am to 3:30pm. Check the gallery’s current booking details before making it your first day.
picks.label: Check the studio tour

picks.headline: One farm, a Halloween afternoon
picks.body: The Big Goose’s Halloweekend is listed for 31 October and 1 November, with Golden Pumpkins and a costume parade. Check the operator’s programme and make this the family day’s anchor.
picks.label: Check the family programme

editorial.body: Sorrento works as a base when you give the village some time. Our weekend story is the companion to a slower stay, with the bay and back beach shaping the day rather than another trip up the ridge.
editorial.label: Explore the Sorrento story
